title: Biba op-art mini-dress
lede: A long-sleeved jersey mini-dress from the London boutique Biba, printed with nested diamonds in brown and black.
summary: A high-necked mini-dress in brown jersey with a black print of concentric diamonds. Biba, London, 1965.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the V&A photograph of its copy, T.159-1986 (1040 × 1600 px), on a dress form against a blue backdrop, in a scratchpad. No image is stored.

styles.note: An op print of nested diamonds on a mass-market dress. Partial fit: the colours are brown and black, not black and white.

context: The V&A catalogues the dress with the style “Op art” and says it “was produced during the short lived Op Art fashion trend of 1965”. A horizontal-stripe version was also made. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O133328/).

The V&A notes that “while true optical art was often stark white and black, other colourways were used”, and that Biba used a brown and black textile here. It quotes Barbara Hulanicki on prints that washed out to “faded grey Op-Art print dresses”. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O133328/).
Physical description: straight-cut mini-dress with a high neck and long sleeves, brown jersey with black op-art geometric print, back zip. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O133328/).
observed: The print is a grid of concentric diamonds made of alternating brown and black bands of equal width.
Where four diamond centres meet, the bands turn into small checkerboards, and between them the bands form large X shapes.
The pattern covers the body, sleeves, and roll collar with no plain area.
interpretation: The structure is pure op: one banded unit repeated edge to edge, with checks where the fields meet. The brown ground softens the contrast, so the vibration is weaker than in a black and white print.
The V&A’s own note makes the scope of this style explicit: black and white is the core, and colourways such as this are commercial variants.
borrow: Tile concentric diamonds so that their corners meet and form checkerboards and X shapes between them.
For a softer op field, keep the black and replace the white with one mid-tone.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The V&A photograph is not openly licensed, and the rights in the Biba print are unverified.
